newsitem.title: USA: Barshefsky criticizes Japan response in Kodak case.
newsitem.headline: Barshefsky criticizes Japan response in Kodak case.

text.p: Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky Tuesday criticized Tokyo for placing conditions on a U.S. request to discuss business practices in Japan's photo film market.

The request by the United States to discuss business practices is one aspect of the case before the World Trade Organizaton involving Eastman Kodak Co's complaint that the Japanese government thwarted foreign competition against Fuji Photo Film Co Ltd in Japan.
Japan has said it will consult on the issue if the Americans agree to discuss practices in the U.S. market.

"I am concerned about preserving the integrity of WTO procedures," Barshefsky said in a statement. "A decades-old principle established in the GATT and WTO is that parties should accept a request for consultations in good faith and should not link claims and counterclaims."

A U.S. trade official said Japan's challenge to U.S. business practices in the photo film market is "without merit and is designed simply to divert attention from what is really involved here, which is an inquiry into the Japanese market."
The WTO is set to form a panel on Wednesday to address another aspect of the Kodak case.

The panel, which U.S. officials said will take about 20 days to select, will consider U.S. charges that Tokyo helped establish a distribution system in the film market to block foreign competition and counter its obligations under the old General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade and the WTO.
In a statement, Barshefsky expressed confidence that the United States would win its case, which is expected to take about a year for the panel to decide and parties to appeal any ruling.

"The measures put in place by the government of Japan are a textbook case of a WTO member circumventing its market access obligations," Barshefsky said. "We look forward to having the panel review the full array of Japanese government measures tat are restricting market access in this sector."
